title: TempoPFN: Synthetic Pre-training of Linear RNNs for Zero-shot Time Series Forecasting
claim: A model trained only on synthetically generated and augmented data, then run in parallel, matches or beats models trained on real data.
layout: 3 colored-border panels, left-to-right, blue arrow linking data to model
description: Three side-by-side panels with thick rounded borders in green, orange and blue. The left green panel, 'Synthetic Data', stacks sample time-series plots from the generators. A flow of boxes (TS Mix, Noise, Quant., Scale, Cens., Conv., TS Mix, NaN) applies augmentations, and the augmented series appear below as 'Result'. A thick blue arrow leads into the orange 'Architecture' panel. There, an input series is split by many parallel downward arrows into a central 'TempoPFN Time Series Model' box. More arrows lead out to a forecast with a shaded quantile band over the horizon. The right blue panel, 'GIFT-Eval', shows forecast comparisons for TempoPFN, TiRex and TabPFN-TS. Below them are paired horizontal bars of normalized CRPS and MASE for five models, with colors for real, mixed and synthetic training data. The eye goes first to the large panel titles.
caption: (Left) Synthetic Data Generation pipeline containing a mix of novel and existing time-series generators are augmented with a diverse set of augmentations to produce the time-series used for training. (Middle) The TempoPFN architecture produces coherent quantile predictions for all future time-stamps in parallel. (Right) TempoPFN obtains competitive performance on Gift-Eval despite being trained only on synthetic time-series.
abstract: Foundation models for zero-shot time series forecasting face challenges in efficient long-horizon prediction and reproducibility, with existing synthetic-only approaches underperforming on challenging benchmarks. This paper presents TempoPFN, a univariate time series foundation model based on linear Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) pre-trained exclusively on synthetic data. The model uses a GatedDeltaProduct architecture with state-weaving for fully parallelizable training across sequence lengths, eliminating the need for windowing or summarization techniques while maintaining robust temporal state-tracking. Our comprehensive synthetic data pipeline unifies diverse generators, including stochastic differential equations, Gaussian processes, and audio synthesis, with novel augmentations. In zero-shot evaluations on the Gift-Eval, fev-bench and Chronos-ZS benchmarks, TempoPFN achieves top-tier competitive performance, surpassing the majority of models trained on real-world data, while leveraging fully parallelizable training and inference. We open-source our complete data generation pipeline and training code, providing a reproducible foundation for future research.
